summary.name: PageKite
summary.one_liner: PageKite is an open source localhost tunneling service that makes servers running on your own computer or device reachable on the public Internet via its relay network.
use_cases: Make a home or laptop server publicly reachable
Host WordPress or Nextcloud from home
Test webhooks or APIs on a local machine
Share a work-in-progress site with clients
SSH into devices behind firewalls or NAT
summary.what_it_does: PageKite connects a local server to relays on its network so HTTP, HTTPS, SSH and other TCP-based services can be reached from the public Internet. The pagekite.py or libpagekite tool automatically selects the closest working relay. Traffic passes through the relays, so the home IP address stays hidden, and the firewall can remain closed. It offers stable DNS names, unlimited sub-domains, use of your own domains, and automatic HTTPS, with wildcard relay certificates or end-to-end TLS. The project states it has run since 2010 and is fully managed.
notable: Client tools pagekite.py, libpagekite (C) and upagekite (MicroPython/ESP32)
Relays on four continents with automatic closest-relay selection
Keeps the home IP hidden; all traffic goes through relays
caveats: Free use for individuals is pay-what-you-want, with a suggested $3 USD/month
Subscription, group and embedded plans for professionals start at $5.99 USD/month
Works with HTTP, HTTPS, SSH and a few other TCP-based protocols only
